newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian peso ends higher at 1,010.60.
newsitem.headline: Colombian peso ends higher at 1,010.60.

text.p: Colombia's peso ended 2.0 higher at 1,010.60 on what interbank dealers described as steady dollar sales by oil exporters and the corporate sector.
It was the peso's highest close since October 7 and dealers said the active session saw 342 trades for a total of $147 million.

The peso traded in a 1,009.50 to 1,012.80 range, and dealers said the central bank flashed an electronic alert across trading screens at one point in the day saying it intended to buy dollars at 1,010.20.
There was no evidence the central bank actually intervened to halt the peso's recent gains, however, dealers said.

The central bank, or Banco de la Republica, has come under strong pressure to undercut the peso artificially, since its sharp rise since June makes Colombian goods less competitive abroad and has eroded the real value of export earnings.
But the bank has said repeatedly that it has no intention of altering the peso's daily floating rate exchange band as part of a bid to weaken the local currency.
